column1: # Online rollback: what a snapshot copies and what the state hash covers (PC port request 48, docs/ONLINE_ROLLBACK.md
# 3.3, 3.4, 8.4 and 12.4). Hand-kept; tools/rollback_regions.py resolves it against a link (the build's symbols and
# sections) into <link>/rollback_regions.tsv (address, size, name, kind, snapshot, hash, reason; build.py --port-variant
# publishes out/TM2_SOURCE_PORT/rollback_regions.tsv), and tools/check_rollback.py check 8 proves it: every row
# resolves, and every static word a step's code stores to (the functions portStepBody reaches) lies in a row.
# kind:  range   a section range of the link: game.static = the game's .sdata/.sbss/.bss (retail 801809D4..801FAD48,
#                the relocated build's equivalent), port.bss / port.data = the port variant's .port_bss / .port_data
#        symbol  one symbol of the link; symbol? = the same, skipped when the build does not define it (a port define)
#        fixed   an address range lo-hi of the machine's memory, not of the build (the scratchpad, the port's RAM)
#        field   bytes of every element of an array symbol: size = SYMBOL:STRIDE:LO-HI (request 54: the scene objects'
#                per-view fields); resolved into one row per element, NAME[i]
#        dmd     the models' mutable node fields, listed at run time by portDmdMutableList (not static)
#        ptr     the objects an array of pointers names: size = SYMBOL:WORDS:BYTES (WORDS a count or "next": the words
#                up to the next symbol); resolved into one row per pointer word, NAME[i]:BYTES (address = the word, size
#                0: no static byte); at run time a non-zero word names BYTES at the address it holds, which take the
#                row's snapshot / hash over every static row (request 57: the cameras' scene objects in csObjectPool)
# size:  bytes of a symbol row ("next" = up to the next symbol of the link); lo-hi (hex) of a fixed row; "-" else.
# snapshot: yes = save / load copy it; no = never copied (and never restored). hash: yes = part of the state hash.
# A symbol row inside a range overrides the range for its bytes (a "no" row is a hole in a "yes" range); a symbol
# outside every range (the game's .data) is covered only by its own row. The reason column says why.
# Request 54 (ONLINE_ROLLBACK.md 15.2): "hash yes" is game state only: what the drawing, the interrupts or the sound
# side write (a re-run, with no drawing and SOUND_GATE, does not reproduce them) is "hash no", and "snapshot no" where
# no step reads it; tools/check_rollback.py check 9 proves it for the drawing's static stores and the request's words.
